sentence: This project builds artificial intelligence models that estimate the age of healing fractures in skeletal images of children evaluated for physical abuse.
This project supports cancer research by helping analyze multi-omics data and by building computational resources for retroviral models of cancer.
This project studies how signaling and cell responses set up a stem cell niche, which helps maintain stem cells and tissue renewal.
This project builds a low-cost nanopore RNA sequencing platform to characterize pediatric tumors and tests whether it works in lower-resource settings.
This project develops computational methods that combine physical models with machine learning models to accelerate drug discovery when structural biology data is available.
This project holds a conference on Fragile X Syndrome and autism-related disorders to identify the molecular, cellular and circuit mechanisms behind symptoms.
This project studies how rubella virus disrupts brain development in a developing fetus and causes birth defects.
This project studies how serotonin in the periaqueductal grey changes innate fear responses in adulthood and after developmental interference.
This project tries to find out whether certain cells in mouse kidneys can produce new cells, and whether this differs between males and females.
This project holds a conference to expand collaboration on open-source software for analyzing genomic data, including single-cell, spatial and multi-omic assays.
This project applies dual isotope imaging to study lower extremity flow, nerve activity and calcification of the arteries in peripheral artery disease and diabetes.
This project tests in a clinical trial how sharing genomic risk information with patients and their physicians affects trust, understanding and uptake of recommended interventions.
This project studies how changes in neural stem cell adhesion and migration during aging affect brain repair after injury.
This project studies how the rodent entorhinal cortex sends a signal to the hippocampus that drives learning of specific spatial locations.
This project studies how organs communicate with each other during aging in Drosophila, using single-cell transcriptomics, metabolomics and proteomics.
This project studies how modifiable risk factors affect cognitive performance and decline before Alzheimer’s disease and associated dementias begin.
This project builds open-source methods that measure the molecular contents of individual cells, including under genetic and chemical perturbations.
This project tests whether nutraceuticals and genetically modified bacteria can increase beneficial microbial metabolites to prevent and treat diabetic retinopathy in mouse models.
This project develops computational approaches to analyze large-scale electrophysiological recordings and uncover how several brain areas guide memory-guided movements in Parkinson’s disease.
This project uses genetic data from many individuals to improve polygenic prediction of tobacco and alcohol use across populations.
